A developer in a project that already has a usable Beads Tool Workspace (team or stealth) runs `/use-matt-pocock-workflow` and the agent is handed the `setup-matt-pocock-skills` setup with every answer pre-filled, so they only confirm the draft once.

Sections mirror the upstream GitHub template (issue conventions, "publish to the issue tracker", "fetch the relevant ticket", parent/child via `--parent`, wayfinding operations) with the `bd` commands this repository already uses, and no repository-specific policy (session close, quality gates, shipping docs, glossary references).
- The Beads plugin's guidance policy (`auto`/`off`) is never changed.
- Verify at implementation time: how an extension detects an installed skill at the package's OMP dev-dependency version, and whether a `disable-model-invocation` skill is readable via `skill://` (if not, reference the resolved skill file path).

- [ ] The extension test fixture records `sendUserMessage` calls.
- [ ] Missing setup skill: error names `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`; no `bd` invocation; no message sent.

- [ ] Guidance policy identical before and after.
- [ ] Seed template is included in the package files check.
- [ ] Smoke: in real OMP on a scratch project with Beads ready, the command hands off and the agent produces `docs/agents/*.md` and an `## Agent skills` block in `AGENTS.md` after one confirmation.

title: Matt Pocock Workflow: /use-matt-pocock-workflow command and visual README
description:
## Problem Statement

Setting up a project for the `mattpocock/skills` engineering skills means running `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` and answering the same questions every time: Beads as the issue tracker (which the skill only supports as a freeform "Other" paragraph), the default triage labels, the default single-context domain docs, and `AGENTS.md` as the instructions file. When Beads is not initialized yet, the user must also remember to run `/beads init` first. The answers never change, so repeating them is wasted effort, and the freeform Beads paragraph produces an `issue-tracker.md` of uneven quality.

Separately, a newcomer to this repository cannot quickly see what the plugins do. The root README is a text-and-table reference: the Shared Display's Display Styles, Display Palettes and layouts are described but never shown, and nothing pictures how the packages attach to OMP.

## Solution

A new `/use-matt-pocock-workflow` command, shipped by the Beads plugin, sets a project up as a **Matt Pocock Workflow** in one step:

1. It checks that the `setup-matt-pocock-skills` skill is installed; if not, it stops and tells the user to run `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`.
2. If no usable Beads Tool Workspace exists, it runs the existing Beads initialization in standard/team mode (no mode prompt), still offering the Git hooks choice. A ready workspace, including an existing stealth one, is reused.
3. It hands the setup to the agent: the agent reads the setup skill and follows it with every answer pre-filled (Beads via a shipped seed template, default labels, single-context, always `AGENTS.md`). The skill's own draft-confirmation step stays, so the user confirms once before files are written.

The root README gains a "What it looks like" section: generated images of the Shared Display (Display Styles, Display Palettes, layouts), real images of Caveman, Ponytail and the Context Rail, and mermaid diagrams for the architecture and the non-UI flows (Headroom, RTK, `/use-matt-pocock-workflow`).

## User Stories

1. As a developer starting a new project, I want one command that configures the Matt Pocock Workflow, so that I never re-answer the setup skill's questions.
2. As a developer, I want the command to use Beads as the issue tracker, so that the engineering skills publish and read issues through `bd`.
3. As a developer, I want the default triage labels (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`) applied without a prompt, so that `/triage` works immediately.
4. As a developer, I want the default single-context domain docs layout applied without a prompt, so that `/grill-with-docs` and `/domain-modeling` know where the glossary and ADRs live.
5. As a developer, I want the setup recorded in `AGENTS.md` even when a `CLAUDE.md` exists, so that every agent harness (including Claude Code) reads the same instructions file.
6. As a developer in a project without Beads, I want the command to initialize Beads for me, so that I do not have to remember to run `/beads init` first.
7. As a developer, I want initialization to use standard/team mode without asking, so that the workspace is shared with collaborators through Git.
8. As a developer, I want to still choose whether Git hooks are installed, with "No hooks" listed first, so that hook installation stays opt-in.
9. As a developer whose project already has a ready Beads workspace, I want the command to reuse it without re-initializing, so that my existing issues are untouched.
10. As a developer whose project already has a stealth workspace, I want the command to reuse it rather than force team mode, so that a personal setup is not converted behind my back.
11. As a developer, I want pressing Esc during the hooks choice to stop everything, so that cancelling leaves no half-configured project.
12. As a developer, I want a failed or refused Beads initialization to stop the command before any agent hand-off, so that docs never point at a workspace that does not exist.
13. As a developer without the setup skill installed, I want a clear error with the exact install command (`npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`), so that I can fix it in one step.
14. As a developer without the setup skill installed, I want the command to check for the skill before touching Beads, so that a missing skill never leaves Beads initialized but docs unwritten.
15. As a developer, I want the command to leave the Beads plugin's project guidance policy (`auto`/`off`) unchanged, so that setup never silently changes what the plugin injects into prompts.
16. As a developer, I want the agent to show me the draft `AGENTS.md` block and `docs/agents/*.md` files and wait for one confirmation, so that I can still edit before anything is written.
17. As a developer, I want the generated `issue-tracker.md` to come from a maintained Beads seed template, so that it covers every operation the engineering skills reference with correct `bd` commands.
18. As a developer, I want the Beads template to mirror the sections of the upstream GitHub template (conventions, publishing, fetching, parent/child, wayfinding), so that `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/triage` and `/wayfinder` find the operations they expect.
19. As a developer, I want the Beads template free of this repository's own policies (quality gates, shipping docs, glossary references), so that it fits any project.
20. As a developer, I want existing `docs/agents/*.md` files and an existing `## Agent skills` block handled by the setup skill's own rules, so that the command does not invent a second convention.
21. As a developer, I want the command listed in the Beads plugin README and the root README's command tree, so that I can discover it.
22. As a newcomer to this repository, I want a "What it looks like" section near the top of the README, so that I understand what the plugins do before reading install steps.
23. As a newcomer, I want a diagram showing which OMP surfaces each package attaches to, so that I understand the architecture at a glance.
24. As a prospective user, I want to see each of the four Display Styles (`plain`, `bracketed`, `powerline`, `rounded`) in one shared palette, so that I can choose a shape.
25. As a prospective user, I want to see each of the six Display Palettes (`none`, `theme`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `pastel`, `tokyo-night`) on the same style, so that I can choose colors.
26. As a prospective user, I want to see the horizontal and vertical layouts side by side, so that I can choose a layout.
27. As a prospective user, I want real images of Caveman, Ponytail and the Context Rail, so that I know what they add to my terminal.
28. As a newcomer, I want mermaid diagrams for Headroom compression, RTK command rewriting, and `/use-matt-pocock-workflow`, so that features without a UI are still easy to understand.
29. As a maintainer, I want the Shared Display images generated from the real render code by a re-runnable script, so that the images stay accurate when styles change.
30. As a maintainer, I want the image tooling (`freeze`) to stay a local tool rather than a repository dependency, so that installs and CI are unaffected.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Glossary.** The term **Matt Pocock Workflow** is already recorded in the root glossary. Use it in code names, README text and messages; avoid "skills setup" and "matt setup".
- **Command home.** `/use-matt-pocock-workflow` is a new top-level command registered by the Beads plugin extension, not a `/beads` subcommand. It lives there because it reuses the Beads initialization flow directly.
- **Initialization reuse.** The existing Beads initialization flow gains a way to be called with the mode fixed to standard/team, skipping the mode prompt while keeping the hooks prompt and every existing safety refusal (staged files, dirty root Markdown, project change mid-choice, unusable resulting workspace). The existing "reuse a ready workspace first" behavior is unchanged and applies to stealth workspaces too.
- **Ordering.** Skill presence check → Beads readiness/initialization → agent hand-off. Any failure or cancellation stops before the hand-off.
- **Skill presence.** The command determines whether `setup-matt-pocock-skills` is installed before any side effect. The exact discovery mechanism (OMP extension API vs. skill directories) is decided at implementation time after reading the OMP API at the package's dev-dependency version.
- **Hand-off.** The command sends one user message via `sendUserMessage`. It does not rely on `/skill:` expansion (extension-sent messages bypass slash-command expansion). The message instructs the agent to read the setup skill via `skill://setup-matt-pocock-skills` and to follow it with pre-filled answers: issue tracker = Other/Beads using the shipped seed template (absolute path resolved from the installed package), triage labels = defaults, domain docs = single-context, instructions file = `AGENTS.md` always (create it if missing, never edit `CLAUDE.md`). It keeps the skill's draft-confirmation step. Whether a skill hidden by `disable-model-invocation` is readable via `skill://` must be verified; if it is not, resolve the skill file path and reference it directly.
- **Seed template.** The Beads plugin ships a Beads issue-tracker seed template, included in the published package files. Its sections mirror the upstream GitHub template (conventions/issue operations, "publish to the issue tracker", "fetch the relevant ticket", parent/child via `--parent`, wayfinding operations), using the `bd` commands this repository already uses. It omits repository-specific content (session close, quality gates, shipping docs, glossary references). Upstream (`mattpocock/skills`, checked at commit `5beb35b`) explicitly routes non-GitHub/GitLab/local trackers through "Other" and recommends pointing the setup at a user-maintained file; this template is that file.
- **Policy untouched.** The command never changes the Beads plugin's project guidance policy.
- **README structure.** A "What it looks like" section follows the intro: architecture mermaid, Shared Display image sets (4 Display Styles in `catppuccin`, 6 Display Palettes on `powerline`, horizontal vs. vertical layout; 12 images total), Caveman/Ponytail images, the existing Context Rail preview image, and mermaid flows for Headroom, RTK and `/use-matt-pocock-workflow`. The command tree and the Beads project integration section document the new command. Install reference stays below. README stays in English.
- **Image generation.** A repository script renders Status Segments through the real Shared Display render code to ANSI, then converts to PNG with `freeze` using a local Nerd Font file; output lives with the existing docs assets. `freeze` is a documented local prerequisite for regenerating images only.
- **Release.** Version bump and changelog follow the repository's shipping doc.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests drive the command through its public handler and assert only externally visible effects: `bd` invocations, select prompts shown, notifications, the user message sent, files and policy on disk. They do not assert message wording beyond the decision-carrying content (pre-filled answers, template path).
- One seam: the existing Beads extension test fixture (fake `pi` with `registerCommand`, `exec`, `ui.select`, `notify`), extended with a recording `sendUserMessage`. Prior art: the Beads initialization tests for cancellation, Git auto-commit hazard refusal, and unusable resulting workspace.
- Behaviors to cover:
  1. Missing setup skill → error naming `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills`; no `bd` call; no message sent.
  2. Ready workspace (team or stealth) → no `bd init`; exactly one message containing the pre-filled answers and the template path.
  3. No workspace → no mode prompt; `bd init` invoked without `--stealth`; message sent only after a ready result.
  4. Esc at the hooks choice, a refused init, or an unusable resulting workspace → no message; files, hooks and policy unchanged.
  5. Guidance policy is identical before and after.
- Not tested automatically: whether the agent follows the setup skill correctly (LLM + upstream skill); smoke-test once in real OMP on a scratch project. The README image script and mermaid diagrams are verified by running the script and viewing the output.

## Out of Scope

- Changing or forking the upstream `setup-matt-pocock-skills` skill.
- Supporting issue trackers other than Beads in this command.
- Changing `/beads init`, `/beads auto` or `/beads off` behavior for direct users.
- Converting an existing stealth workspace to team mode.
- Migrating this repository's own `CONTEXT.md` naming to `GLOSSARY.md`.
- Images for all 48 style/palette/layout combinations.
- Translating the README.

## Further Notes

- Upstream setup skill files are byte-identical to the locally installed copy as of `mattpocock/skills@5beb35b` (2026-10-19).
- The hand-off depends on the setup skill's prompt contract; if upstream changes its sections, the pre-filled answers must be revisited.

title: Shared Display: Display Styles + Display Palettes; clean up Ponytail, Headroom, RTK segments
description:
## Problem Statement

The Shared Display under the editor is hard to read and makes working features look broken.

- **Ponytail shows its Mode Level twice.** Its Status Segment renders `○ F___ ponytail: ⚡ FULL`. The user's animated glyph already spells out the Mode Level (`F___` → `FULL`), and the static `⚡ FULL` repeats it.
- **Headroom looks dead.** The segment shows `💾 0% (0 saved)` from the moment the proxy is reachable, before anything has been compressed.
  - The `compressed` state is chosen whenever the proxy is online, so the `online` state is never shown.
  - Headroom Savings as a percent sits at 0–1% almost all the time. Its denominator is every token of every request in the Agent Session, while only a few tool results can be compressed. The proxy's own aggregate is about 1.25%.
  - The user cannot tell what either number means. Neither one visibly moves, so the user concluded Headroom does not work.
- **RTK looks dead.** The segment shows `rtk 💾 0% (0 saved)`. RTK is working, but its guards (ADR-0007) skip most commands an agent runs: about 75% are skipped for containing a pipe. Few commands get rewritten, so the numbers stay at zero.
  - The display cannot distinguish "no command went through rtk yet" from "rtk is broken".
- **Headroom and RTK look identical.** Both segments use the same `💾 N% (N saved)` shape, so the user cannot tell them apart.
- **Too few looks.** The display offers only `plain` and theme-colored `powerline`. The user wants the range of looks Starship's prompt presets offer, and wants to change the colors independently of the shape.

## Solution

**Clean up the Display Producers:**
- **Ponytail.** Drops the static Mode Level text and its placeholders entirely. Each Mode Level gets its own packaged glyph, so the Mode Level shows through the glyph. Users who want text put it in their own glyph files.
- **Headroom.** Shows `✓ Headroom` while online with nothing saved yet. Once tokens are saved it shows `Headroom 12.4k saved`. Percent placeholders stay available to users who want them.
- **RTK.** Shows tokens saved plus the number of commands that went through rtk, for example `rtk 3.2k saved · 4 cmds`. `0 cmds` reads as idle, not broken. The guards are unchanged.

**Shared Display gains two independent settings, both selectable in `/omp-plugins`:**
- **Display Style** sets the shape, with four values: `plain`, `bracketed`, `powerline`, `rounded`. These cover every Starship preset whose look can apply to a status surface without rewriting segment content. Presets whose shape differs in only one detail were merged into one style.
- **Display Palette** sets the colors, with six values: `none`, `theme`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `pastel`, `tokyo-night`.

## User Stories

1. As an OMP user, I want Ponytail's Status Segment to show its Mode Level only once, so that the display is not redundant.
2. As an OMP user with animated Ponytail glyphs, I want my glyph to be the only place the Mode Level appears, so that the animation carries the meaning.
3. As an OMP user without custom Ponytail glyphs, I want the packaged glyph to differ per Mode Level (`🐴🌿` lite, `🐴⚡` full, `🐴🔥` ultra), so that I can still tell which Mode Level is active.
4. As an OMP user, I want to put any Mode Level text or icon I like into my own Ponytail glyph files, so that I fully control how the Mode Level looks.
5. As an OMP user, I want the Ponytail activity dot (`●` running, `○` idle) to remain, so that I can still see whether the agent is working.
6. As an OMP user, I want Headroom's Status Segment to say "Headroom" by default, so that I can tell it apart from RTK.
7. As an OMP user, I want Headroom to show `✓ Headroom` while the proxy is reachable but nothing has been saved yet, so that zero values don't look like a failure.
8. As an OMP user, I want Headroom to show the tokens it saved this Agent Session in compact form (such as `12.4k`), so that I see a number that visibly grows.
9. As an OMP user, I want Headroom to switch from the online look to the saved look as soon as the first token is saved, so that the change itself signals that compression worked.
10. As an OMP user who prefers percentages, I want Headroom's percent placeholders to stay available in my own template, so that I can still show Headroom Savings as a share.
11. As an OMP user, I want RTK's Status Segment to show tokens saved this Agent Session in compact form, so that I see a number that visibly grows.
12. As an OMP user, I want RTK to show how many commands went through rtk this Agent Session, so that I can tell "nothing rewritten yet" from "broken".
13. As an OMP user, I want RTK and Headroom to stop sharing the same icon and number shape, so that the two segments are distinguishable at a glance.
14. As an OMP user, I want to choose a Display Style for the Shared Display, so that it matches the look of my terminal prompt.
15. As an OMP user, I want a `plain` Display Style that joins segments with my configured separator, so that I keep a minimal look like Starship's Pure or Jetpack presets.
16. As an OMP user, I want a `bracketed` Display Style that wraps each segment in `[ ]`, so that I get the look of Starship's Bracketed Segments preset.
17. As an OMP user, I want a `powerline` Display Style with a rounded start cap, arrow separators and a rounded end cap, so that I get the look of Starship's Gruvbox Rainbow, Catppuccin Powerline and Pastel Powerline presets.
18. As an OMP user, I want a `rounded` Display Style with a `░▒▓` gradient start and rounded separators and end cap, so that I get the look of Starship's Tokyo Night preset.
19. As an OMP user, I want to choose a Display Palette independently of the Display Style, so that I can combine any shape with any colors.
20. As an OMP user, I want a `theme` Display Palette that follows my OMP theme's status-line colors, so that the Shared Display matches the rest of OMP.
21. As an OMP user, I want `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `pastel` and `tokyo-night` Display Palettes with the original Starship preset colors, so that I get those familiar color schemes.
22. As an OMP user, I want a `none` Display Palette, so that segments render without any added color.
23. As an OMP user using `plain` or `bracketed`, I want segment text colored by the palette's text colors, which are readable on a dark terminal, so that dark background shades never become unreadable text.
24. As an OMP user using `plain` or `bracketed` with a palette other than `none`, I want the palette to color each segment's text in order, so that segments are visually separated.
25. As an OMP user using `powerline` or `rounded`, I want each segment painted with the palette's background and text colors in order, so that segments read as colored blocks.
26. As an OMP user using `theme` with an OMP theme that does not resolve true colors, I want the Shared Display to fall back to uncolored plain rendering, so that it never renders broken colors.
27. As an OMP user using the vertical layout, I want each segment on its own row decorated by the chosen Display Style and Display Palette, so that vertical mode matches horizontal mode.
28. As an OMP user, I want the separator setting to apply only to `plain`, so that styles with built-in separators are never double-separated.
29. As an OMP user, I want a `Palette` selector next to `Style` in `/omp-plugins`, so that I can change colors where I change the shape.
30. As an OMP user, I want style and palette changes to apply live to the Shared Display, so that I can preview a combination by selecting it.
31. As an OMP user, I want an invalid style or palette in my Root Plugin Configuration to fall back to the defaults, so that a typo never breaks the display.
32. As an OMP user, I want a Display Style never to change a producer's own icons or text, so that each feature's segment content stays under that feature's control.
33. As a plugin maintainer, I want Display Styles and Display Palettes owned only by the Display Host, so that Display Producers stay independent of composition (ADR-0003).
34. As a plugin maintainer, I want Display Style and Display Palette defined in the glossary, so that issues and code use one vocabulary.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Glossary.** `CONTEXT.md` now defines Display Style (shape only: caps, separators, brackets, padding; no colors; never changes segment content) and Display Palette (named colors chosen independently of the style).

**Shared Display (Display Host)**

- **Display Configuration.** `sharedDisplay.style` becomes `plain | bracketed | powerline | rounded`, default `plain`. New `sharedDisplay.palette` is `none | theme | gruvbox | catppuccin | pastel | tokyo-night`, default `theme`. Normalization replaces unknown values with defaults. Validation in `/omp-plugins` rejects unknown values.
- **Composition options.** Composition takes a style plus a resolved palette instead of the current optional powerline palette. The Display Host resolves the palette. `theme` resolves from the OMP theme's status-line colors exactly as the current powerline does. If it cannot resolve true colors, rendering falls back to uncolored `plain`, which preserves current behavior.
- **Palette data shape.**
  - Segment colors are an ordered list of background/foreground pairs, cycled per segment. Tokyo Night needs a different foreground per segment.
  - A separate ordered list of text-only colors is used by `plain` and `bracketed`.
  - Colors come from Starship's original preset TOML files:
    - **gruvbox** (gruvbox_dark): backgrounds `#d65d0e #d79921 #689d6a #458588 #665c54 #3c3836`, text `#fbf1c7`. The text-only list drops the two dark neutrals.
    - **catppuccin** (mocha only): backgrounds `#f38ba8 #fab387 #f9e2af #a6e3a1 #74c7ec #b4befe`, text `#11111b`. The text-only list reuses the accents.
    - **pastel**: backgrounds `#9A348E #DA627D #FCA17D #86BBD8 #06969A #33658A`. The original leaves foreground unset, so text uses the terminal default foreground.
    - **tokyo-night**: pairs `#a3aed2/#090c0c`, `#769ff0/#e3e5e5`, `#394260/#769ff0`, `#212736/#769ff0`, `#1d2230/#a0a9cb`. Text-only colors `#a3aed2 #769ff0 #e3e5e5 #a0a9cb`.
    - **theme**: backgrounds from the theme status-line colors and text from the theme's status-line background (current powerline behavior). The text-only list is the theme status-line colors.
    - **none**: no colors.
- **Style shapes (horizontal).**
  - `plain`: segments joined by `horizontalSeparator`.
  - `bracketed`: each segment wrapped in `[`…`]`, adjacent with no separator.
  - `powerline`: start cap U+E0B6, arrow U+E0B0 between segments, end cap U+E0B4. This is the current powerline shape.
  - `rounded`: `░▒▓` start in the first segment's color, U+E0B4 between segments and at the end.
  - `powerline` and `rounded` need a Nerd Font. `plain` and `bracketed` do not.
- **Producer colors.** Whenever a palette other than `none` applies, producer SGR colors are stripped so palette colors win, as powerline does today. With `none`, producer output is rendered untouched.
- **Separator.** `horizontalSeparator` applies to `plain` only.
- **Vertical layout.** Each segment occupies its own rows. Each row is decorated as a one-segment instance of the chosen style with the segment's palette color, generalizing current powerline vertical behavior.
- **Settings UI.** `/omp-plugins` adds a `Palette` select next to `Style`. `Style` lists the four styles. Descriptions note the Nerd Font requirement. There is no preview surface; live config change already re-renders.

**Ponytail (Display Producer)**

- The template supports only `{activity}` and `{glyph}`. `{mode}`, `{modeIcon}` and the mode-icon table are removed with no backward compatibility. An old template containing them renders the placeholder text literally.
- The default template becomes `{activity} {glyph} ponytail`.
- Packaged assets per Mode Level are lite `🐴🌿`, full `🐴⚡` and ultra `🐴🔥`. off and review keep `🐴`.
- This is a breaking change for Ponytail templates (major version bump).

**Headroom (Display Producer)**

- The widget-state decision gains whether the Agent Session has saved any tokens. With the proxy online it returns `online` when saved tokens are 0 and `compressed` when greater than 0. The other states are unchanged.
- The default `compressed` template becomes `{glyph} Headroom {tokensSaved} saved`, with `tokensSaved` in compact form (`950`, `12.4k`, `3.4M`). The `online` default stays `{glyph} Headroom`. Percent placeholders (`{compressionPercent}`, `{lastPercent}`) remain supported. The definition of Headroom Savings is unchanged.

**RTK (Display Producer)**

- The default template becomes `{glyph} rtk {tokensSaved} saved · {commands} cmds`. `{commands}` already exists and counts rows recorded in the Agent Session's history.
- Guards and the ADR-0007 policy are unchanged.

**Housekeeping**

- Package versions are bumped per AGENTS.md in every touched package: shared-display, ponytail, headroom, rtk and codesook-omp-plugin.
- Package READMEs or docs describing templates, placeholders or styles are updated.

## Testing Decisions

**What makes a good test here:**
- It asserts consumer-visible output: rendered Shared Display rows for a given Display Configuration and producer snapshots, or the snapshot text a producer publishes for a given state.
- It never asserts internal helpers, ANSI-building internals beyond what a user sees, or config wiring.
- Expected rows may be compared after stripping SGR for shape, plus targeted checks that the expected 24-bit color codes appear for palette assertions.

**Shared Display.** Use the existing host harness (`makeHostHarness` in the shared-display test suite). Extend the harness with a fake OMP theme exposing status-line colors; this extends the harness and adds no new seam. Cover:
- Each of the 4 styles in horizontal layout (shape: caps, separators, brackets).
- The palette being applied: a fixed palette's colors appear; `none` adds no SGR; `theme` uses theme colors.
- The `theme` fallback to uncolored plain when the theme lacks true colors.
- The separator applying only to `plain`.
- Vertical layout decoration per segment.
- Normalization of unknown style and palette values to the defaults.

**Ponytail.** Use the existing extension harness (`createHarness`, "Ponytail display" tests). Assert:
- The default published snapshot no longer contains Mode Level text.
- The packaged glyph differs per Mode Level.
- `{mode}`/`{modeIcon}` are no longer substituted.

**Headroom.** Use the existing display test suite (widget-state and frame-rendering functions). Headroom has no extension-level harness, and the maintainer chose not to add one. Assert:
- Online with no savings selects `online` and renders `Headroom` without numbers.
- Online with savings selects `compressed` and renders compact tokens saved.
- Update the existing widget-state expectation.

**RTK.** Use the existing extension fixture (snapshot strings). Update the existing default-template expectations (currently `✂ rtk 0% (0 saved)` / `✂ rtk 80% (800 saved)`) to the new tokens-and-commands form.

**`/omp-plugins` settings.** No permanent test, because the Palette select is wiring. Verify with a smoke run of the settings surface.

**Prior art.**
- shared-display "Shared Display source composition" and "Shared Display configuration" suites.
- ponytail "Ponytail display" suite.
- headroom "Headroom display producer" suite.
- rtk extension snapshot tests.

## Out of Scope

- Relaxing RTK's pipe or other guards. That reopens ADR-0007 and carries output-safety risk.
- Headroom re-sending the whole conversation to the proxy on nearly every call (tracked separately as omp-plugins-1kf).
- User-defined hex palettes. Only named palettes are in scope.
- Catppuccin flavors other than mocha.
- Starship's Nerd Font Symbols, No Nerd Fonts and Plain Text Symbols presets. They only swap module icons, which a Display Style may not do.
- No Runtime Versions and No Empty Icons presets. They change module content this display does not have.
- Any style-driven change to a producer's icons or text. That would require a new ADR superseding ADR-0003's ownership split.
- A style preview UI.
- Migrating existing users' Root Plugin Configuration templates. Explicit templates in a user's config keep overriding the new defaults.
- Changing Headroom percent precision or the definition of Headroom Savings or RTK Savings.

## Further Notes

**Diagnosis behind the Headroom and RTK changes (from session replay and live probes):**
- **Headroom proxy works.** A 28k-character log compressed to 43 tokens.
- **Headroom saves nothing on most tool results.** The server returns 0 savings for `read`, `grep`, `edit`, `write`, `task` and similar results. It saves on `bash`, `eval`, `fetch`, `ssh` and MCP or unknown tools.
- **RTK is installed and tracking.** `rtk` 0.51.0 is installed and tracking works. Of 326 bash calls (Oct 21–23), 245 hit the pipe guard and only 18 were rewritten.
- The maintainer's own Root Plugin Configuration sets explicit `ponytail.template`, `headroom.status.compressed` and `rtk.template` values. Those must be updated by hand to see the new defaults.
- Starship preset sources: https://starship.rs/presets.

title: skill-stats: record Skill Uses with /skill-stats dashboards
description:
## Problem Statement

The user has many skills installed: 63 managed by `npx skills`, plus project skills, plugin skills and managed skills. They want to delete the ones they don't use, but nothing records which skills are used, how often, or by whom. Some skills are used only when the agent reads them on its own, so the user's memory of typing `/skill:x` is not a reliable guide. Deleting by guess risks removing something the agent relies on.

## Solution

A new `skill-stats` feature records every Skill Use and attributes it to its source: the user, the agent on its own, or a subagent.

- **Dashboards.** `/skill-stats` opens a dashboard for Global Skills. `/skill-stats project` opens one for the current project's Project Skills. Each shows weekly (7-day), monthly (30-day) and total counts, last-used dates, every installed skill including those never used, and a "delete candidates" section with a ready-to-copy removal command.
- **Reset.** `/skill-stats reset` starts counting again, for all skills or for one, without deleting history.
- **Import.** `/skill-stats import` fills in usage from existing session history once.

## User Stories

1. As an OMP user, I want every time a skill is used to be recorded automatically, so that I have real data before deleting anything.
2. As an OMP user, I want uses I trigger myself with `/skill:name` recorded with source `user`, so that I can tell my own habits apart from the agent's.
3. As an OMP user, I want uses where the agent reads a skill on its own recorded with source `agent`, so that skills the agent depends on don't look unused.
4. As an OMP user, I want uses inside subagents recorded with source `subagent`, so that skills loaded only by task agents are visible.
5. As an OMP user, I want every read to count, including reads of a skill's sub-files, so that the numbers reflect how much each skill is used.
6. As an OMP user, I want Ponytail's helper commands (`/ponytail-review`, `/ponytail-audit`, `/ponytail-debt`) recorded as Skill Uses, so that skills sent as plain text are not missed.
7. As an OMP user, I want uses on branches I later abandon still counted, so that every use that happened is kept.
8. As an OMP user, I want a use counted against the skill that was actually loaded, so that a Project Skill overriding a Global Skill of the same name is counted where it really came from.
9. As an OMP user, I want to run `/skill-stats` and see every Global Skill with its 7-day, 30-day and total counts and its last-used date, so that I can judge each skill.
10. As an OMP user, I want each count broken down by source (user, agent, subagent), so that I understand why a skill is used.
11. As an OMP user, I want installed skills with zero uses listed too, so that the skills I have never used are the most visible.
12. As an OMP user, I want the least-used skills sorted to the top, so that deletion candidates come first.
13. As an OMP user, I want each Global Skill's origin shown (npx-skills managed, plugin, managed, home directory), so that I know how it could be removed.
14. As an OMP user, I want to run `/skill-stats project` and see the same dashboard for the current project's Project Skills, so that project-specific skills are judged on their own.
15. As an OMP user, I want Project Skill statistics stored in the project folder, so that they travel with the project.
16. As an OMP user, I want the project's statistics kept out of Git automatically, so that every skill use doesn't show up as a change for my team.
17. As an OMP user, I want Global Skill statistics stored once per machine, across all projects, so that the global dashboard reflects all my work.
18. As an OMP user, I want a "delete candidates" section listing skills unused for 60 days or more, so that I get a short list to act on.
19. As an OMP user, I want skills installed less than 60 days ago excluded from delete candidates, so that a skill I just added is not recommended for removal.
20. As an OMP user, I want the candidates section to show one combined `npx skills remove -g …` command on the global dashboard, so that I can remove them all in one step.
21. As an OMP user, I want the project dashboard to show `npx skills remove …` without `-g`, for skills in the project's `.agents/skills`, so that the command removes from the right scope.
22. As an OMP user, I want the generated command to omit `-y`, so that `npx skills` still asks me before deleting.
23. As an OMP user, I want to press `c` to copy the removal command to the clipboard, so that I can paste it into a shell.
24. As an OMP user, I want candidates that `npx skills` did not install to show their path instead of joining the command, so that the command never targets something it cannot remove.
25. As an OMP user, I want `/skill-stats reset` to start counting again for all skills, so that I can measure from a fresh point.
26. As an OMP user, I want `/skill-stats reset <skill>` to start counting again for one skill, so that I can re-evaluate a single skill.
27. As an OMP user, I want a confirmation before any reset, so that I don't reset by accident.
28. As an OMP user, I want reset to keep the history and only move the Reset Point, so that a mistaken reset loses nothing.
29. As an OMP user, I want the dashboards' total to mean "since the last Reset Point", so that the numbers match what I reset.
30. As an OMP user, I want `/skill-stats import` to read my existing OMP session history and record the Skill Uses it finds, so that the dashboards are useful on day one.
31. As an OMP user, I want import to run without any model call, so that it costs no tokens.
32. As an OMP user, I want import to run only once and to say so if I run it again, so that history is never counted twice.
33. As an OMP user, I want import to cover only history from before recording started, so that live-recorded uses are not duplicated.
34. As an OMP user, I want imported Project Skill uses written into their own project folder when that folder still exists, so that project dashboards are filled too.
35. As an OMP user, I want import to be all-or-nothing, so that a failure partway does not leave half-imported data that blocks a retry.
36. As an OMP user, I want import to report how many sessions and Skill Uses it read, so that I know it worked.
37. As an OMP user, I want skills whose instruction file no longer exists on disk hidden from the dashboards, so that removed skills stop cluttering the list.
38. As an OMP user, I want a skill that is just not visible from the current project to stay listed, unlike a removed one, so that switching projects never hides the history of skills that still exist.
39. As an OMP user without a UI, I want `/skill-stats` to print the same tables as plain text, so that the command still works in print or RPC mode.
40. As an OMP user, I want statistics kept indefinitely, so that long-term trends are available.

## Implementation Decisions

- **New feature.** Named `skill-stats`, a new workspace package exposed as an omp-plugins root feature. It registers `/skill-stats` with the arguments `project`, `reset [skill]` and `import`.
- **Skill Use detection (live), all inside the extension, with no OMP core change:**
  - **User source.** A message whose custom type is the skill-prompt type and whose attribution is the user. The skill's name and path come from the message details.
  - **Subagent source.** A skill-prompt message without user attribution, in a subagent's session (autoloaded skills), plus any skill read inside a subagent session.
  - **Agent source.** A read tool call whose path, or one of its listed paths, is a `skill://` URI, and a bash tool call whose command contains a `skill://` URI, in the main agent.
  - Every occurrence counts. Sub-file reads count. Abandoned branches count.
  - The skill is identified by the path that was actually loaded.
- **Ponytail helpers.** The Ponytail feature records its helper commands as Skill Uses with source `user`, through a small contract the skill-stats feature exposes on the shared event bus. This keeps the two features independent: if skill-stats is not loaded, nothing happens.
- **Project versus Global.**
  - A Project Skill's instruction file lives inside the Integration Project, for example in its `.omp/skills`, `.agents/skills` or `.claude/skills`.
  - Every other skill is a Global Skill: home directories, managed skills, plugin-provided skills.
- **Installed skill list.**
  - Comes from OMP's command list for skill commands, giving name, description and path.
  - The origin is `npx-skills` when the skill is in the `npx skills` global lock file, which also supplies `installedAt`. For Project Skills, `npx-skills` applies when the skill sits in the project's `.agents/skills`.
  - Other origins are `plugin`, `managed` and `home`.
  - Install time falls back to the instruction file's modification time.
- **Storage.**
  - Global: a per-machine store under the Codesook data directory, next to RTK's data.
  - Project: a store inside the Integration Project's `.omp/skill-stats/` directory, which contains its own ignore-everything Git ignore file.
  - Each record holds the skill name, the loaded path, the source, the Agent Session id, the project, and a timestamp.
  - The store must tolerate several OMP processes appending at once. An append-only log or SQLite both satisfy this; pick the simpler one during implementation.
  - Records are never deleted.
  - Each store also keeps its Reset Points (one global, plus one per skill) and, for import, the recording start time and an "imported" flag.
- **Reports.**
  - Counts within the last 7 days, the last 30 days, and since the applicable Reset Point (the later of the global and per-skill points), plus last used, each split by source.
  - All installed skills are listed, including those with zero uses. Rows are sorted ascending by the since-reset count, then by oldest last use.
  - Skills whose recorded instruction file no longer exists are hidden.
  - A skill that exists but is not currently discovered stays listed.
- **Delete candidates.**
  - Rule: no use in the last 60 days, and installed at least 60 days ago.
  - The command line is `npx skills remove -g <names…>` on the global dashboard, or `npx skills remove <names…>` on the project dashboard, never with `-y`.
  - It includes only skills with the `npx-skills` origin. The others show their paths.
  - `c` copies the command to the clipboard: OSC 52, with the platform clipboard tool as a fallback.
- **Reset.** After confirmation, it writes a Reset Point (global, or for the named skill) in the store of the dashboard's scope. No record is removed.
- **Import.**
  - One-shot. It refuses if the store is already marked imported.
  - It streams OMP's session history files, including subagent transcripts beside each session, parsing line by line because entries can be very large.
  - It extracts the same three signals as live detection, from skill-prompt entries and from tool execution start entries for `read` and `bash`.
  - It takes only entries older than the recording start time.
  - It writes Project Skill uses into their project store only when that folder still exists.
  - It commits each store in one step, then marks it imported.
  - It uses no model calls.
- **No-UI mode.** Every subcommand prints plain text.

## Testing Decisions

- **What a good test is.** Feed the extension the same events OMP sends and run the real command. Assert what the user sees (overlay and plain-text tables, the generated removal command, confirmations) and what lands on disk (store contents in a disposable HOME and project).   - A same-name override is counted to the loaded path.
  - Project versus Global classification.
  - The 7, 30, 60-day boundaries.
  - Zero-use skills are listed.
  - Sort order.
  - Hiding by missing file versus keeping by non-discovery.
  - Global and per-skill Reset Points, and that reset deletes nothing.
  - Import runs once, respects the recording start time, and is all-or-nothing.
  - Import writes Project Skill uses to the right project and skips missing folders.

- Any model or LLM involvement, including in import.

title: beads: Ready Issue counts in segment and /beads tasks live view
description:
## Problem Statement

The Beads Status Segment says only `Beads: ready`. That word means the Beads integration is usable (a Ready Integration), but users read it as "there is work ready". It tells the user nothing about how much work is left. Seeing the tasks means leaving OMP or asking the agent, and asking the agent spends a turn. The segment also refreshes only when a turn starts, so after the user changes issues from another terminal, it stays stale until the next prompt.

## Solution

The Beads feature shows the count of Ready Issues and open issues in its Status Segment, for example `Beads: 5 ready · 12 open`, whenever any open issues exist. When there are none, it shows the integration state as before. A new live view opened with `/beads tasks`, or with "Show tasks" in the `/beads` menu, lists the open issues grouped by status with a short description, and updates itself while open. Both the segment and the view refresh when Beads writes data, not only when a turn starts.

## User Stories

1. As an OMP user in a project with Beads, I want the Status Segment to show how many Ready Issues and open issues exist, so that I know how much work is left without asking.
2. As an OMP user, I want the segment to say `ready` only for Ready Issues, and to keep showing the integration state when there are no open issues, so that the two meanings of "ready" never mix.
3. As an OMP user, I want open issues to include in-progress and blocked ones but not deferred ones, so that deliberately postponed work does not inflate the count.
4. As an OMP user, I want to change the segment's wording through a template with `{ready}`, `{open}` and `{inProgress}` tokens, like other segments, so that it fits my status line.
5. As an OMP user, I want the default template to be `Beads: {ready} ready · {open} open`, so that it is useful without configuration.
6. As an OMP user, I want the existing visibility settings (`ready`, `always`, `never`) and project overrides to keep working, so that my configuration stays valid.
7. As an OMP user, I want the segment to update shortly after Beads data changes, including changes I make from another terminal, so that the numbers are not stale between turns.
8. As an OMP user, I want those updates to cost nothing while Beads data is unchanged, so that an idle session doesn't keep spawning `bd`.
9. As an OMP user, I want to run `/beads tasks` to open a live list of open issues, so that I can see what is left without leaving OMP.
10. As an OMP user, I want "Show tasks" in the `/beads` menu, so that I can find the view without remembering the argument.
11. As an OMP user, I want the list grouped as in progress, ready, and blocked, so that I see what is moving, what I can start, and what is stuck.
12. As an OMP user, I want each row to show the issue id, priority, title, and the first line of its description, so that I can recognize the work at a glance.
13. As an OMP user, I want issues sorted by priority within each group, so that the most important work is on top.
14. As an OMP user, I want long titles and descriptions truncated to the terminal width, so that the list stays readable.
15. As an OMP user, I want to scroll the list with the arrow keys when it is longer than the screen, so that I can see every issue.
16. As an OMP user, I want the open view to update itself when Beads data changes, so that it stays live while I watch.
17. As an OMP user, I want the view to be read-only and close with Enter/Esc without touching my prompt input, so that opening it can never change issues or interrupt work.
18. As an OMP user, I want a clear empty state when there are no open issues, so that I can tell "nothing left" apart from "failed to load".
19. As an OMP user, I want a clear message when Beads is uninitialized, missing, suppressed, or erroring, so that the view explains why it has no list.
20. As an OMP user without a UI, I want `/beads tasks` to return the same grouped list as plain text, so that the command still works in print or RPC mode.
21. As a collaborator in a repo with a Suppressed Integration, I want the counts and the view to respect suppression in the same way the existing status does, so that project policy is honored.
22. As an OMP user, I want the agent never to create or modify issues because of this view, so that the On-demand Beads Workflow still holds.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Scope.** This extends the existing Beads feature package. No new package.
- **Counts.** They come from `bd` in read-only, sandboxed mode (the same flags inspection uses today), with the existing timeout and the stale-result guard.
  - A Ready Issue is an open issue with no open blocker, as reported by `bd`.
  - Open means every status that is not closed and not deferred.
  - In-progress is counted separately for the template.
- **Segment.**
  - When the inspection state is ready and the open count is above zero, it renders the template.
  - In every other state it renders today's `Beads: <state>` text.
  - It adds a `display.beads.template` key to Display Configuration, with tokens `{ready}`, `{open}` and `{inProgress}`.
  - Visibility rules are unchanged.
- **Change signal.** The feature watches Beads' own write markers inside the Tool Workspace: the last-touched marker and the export state. Their modification time changes only when Beads writes issue data.
  - On a change it runs a debounced refresh, in addition to the existing turn-start and command triggers.
  - The watch is created for a Ready Integration only and is torn down on session shutdown and project switch.
  - There is no timer-based polling.
  - This replaces the README statement that the feature has no idle watcher.
- **Live view.**
  - A Read-only Status Overlay with a scrollable list.
  - Data comes from `bd`'s JSON issue listing for non-closed, non-deferred issues, with no limit.
  - Rows are grouped into in_progress, ready and blocked. Blocked means open but not ready.
  - Rows are sorted by priority, and then by most recently updated.
  - It re-queries on the change signal while open.
  - Enter/Esc closes it. No input is captured.
  - The `/beads` command gains a `tasks` argument and a "Show tasks" menu entry. Argument completion includes `tasks`.
- **No-UI mode.** `/beads tasks` prints the same grouping as plain text.
- **Terminology.** User-facing text uses "ready" only for Ready Issues in the counted form. The integration state words stay as they are for the non-counted states.

## Testing Decisions

- **What a good test is.** Drive the extension through events and the `/beads` command. Assert the published segment text, overlay and plain-text output, and which `bd` invocations were issued. Never assert internal parsing helpers.
- **Seam.** The extension's default export with a fake `pi`: events, commands, the event bus, and an `exec` answering `bd` commands with fixture JSON. Use a disposable project with a `.beads` directory whose marker files the test touches to trigger the change signal, and an injected clock for the debounce.
- **Cases to cover:**
  - The template renders when open issues are above zero.
  - The fallback to state text at zero and in non-ready states.
  - Deferred issues are excluded.
  - The visibility and project overrides are still honored.
  - A marker change triggers exactly one refresh, and no change triggers none.
  - The watch is torn down on shutdown.
  - Grouping, ordering and truncation in the view.
  - Empty and error states.
  - The no-UI output.
  - No write-capable `bd` command is ever issued.
- **Prior art.** The existing Beads extension and command-menu tests, which already use `bd` exec fixtures and assert `Beads: …` strings. They will need updating where the segment text changes.
- **Smoke proof.** Use the `verify-omp-plugins` skill. Add a Beads feature entry that drives `/beads tasks` in a scratch project with seeded issues.

## Out of Scope

- Claiming, closing, editing or creating issues from the view.
- Polling `bd` on a timer.
- Showing closed or deferred issues.
- Changes to how the Beads integration is detected or initialized.
- Beads data from other projects.

## Further Notes

- Glossary terms used: Ready Integration, Ready Issue, Status Segment, Shared Display, Read-only Status Overlay, Integration Project, Tool Workspace, Suppressed Integration, On-demand Beads Workflow.
- This is second in the suggested build order (process-monitor, Beads live view, skill-stats). There are no hard dependencies.
- Bump the Beads package version. Update its README, which currently says there is no idle watcher.

title: process-monitor: /procs dashboard for Leftover Processes and ports
description:
## Problem Statement

OMP often starts web servers and other long-running processes while it works, for example a dev server to check a page, a preview server, or a browser for the browser tool. When the work is done, these processes are often left running and keep holding their ports. The user finds out only when a later command fails with "port already in use". By then the Agent Session that started the process is gone, and nothing says which process came from OMP, which session started it, or whether it is safe to stop.

On the user's machine today, a headless Chromium started by the browser tool for another project has been running for 8 days. There are 27 listening TCP ports, and none of them can be traced back to OMP from the process environment.

## Solution

A new `process-monitor` feature adds:
- a `/procs` command that opens a Read-only Status Overlay listing every process OMP started, across all projects, with its ports, command, owning Agent Session, and whether that session has ended (a Leftover Process);
- per-PID kill of processes proven to come from OMP, with a confirmation every time;
- a Status Segment in the Shared Display, such as `⚠ 2 ports`, shown only while Leftover Processes are holding ports;
- a prompt when an Agent Session ends, listing the processes it started that are still running and offering to close them. When OMP quits and there is no UI left to ask, the next OMP start reports them instead.

So that processes started from the bash tool can be attributed after OMP exits, the feature tags every bash tool command with the Agent Session it ran in (ADR-0010).

## User Stories

1. As an OMP user, I want to run `/procs` and see every long-running process OMP started, so that I know what is still running after my work is done.
2. As an OMP user, I want each process row to show its PID, the TCP ports it listens on, its command, its project, and the Agent Session that started it, so that I can tell what it is and where it came from.
3. As an OMP user, I want processes whose Agent Session has ended to be marked as Leftover Processes, so that I can see at a glance what was forgotten.
4. As an OMP user, I want processes holding a listening port to be highlighted, so that I can find the one blocking the port I need.
5. As an OMP user, I want processes from every project on the machine listed, with the current project first, so that I also find leftovers from other projects, like a browser left running for days.
6. As an OMP user, I want OMP's own internal processes, such as the daemon broker and eval workers, in a separate collapsed group, so that they don't crowd out my servers but stay inspectable.
7. As an OMP user, I want every other listening port on the machine shown in an "unknown origin" group, so that I can still find a port holder that OMP cannot prove it started.
8. As an OMP user, I want the unknown-origin group to be view-only, so that I never kill an unrelated program by mistake.
9. As an OMP user, I want to kill a selected OMP-attributed process from the overlay, so that I can free its port without leaving OMP.
10. As an OMP user, I want a confirmation that names the PID, command and ports before every kill, so that I don't stop the wrong process.
11. As an OMP user, I want kills to target one PID and never a process name, so that other instances of the same program are untouched.
12. As an OMP user, I want the overlay to refresh after a kill, so that I can see the process is gone and the port is free.
13. As an OMP user, I want the overlay to report clearly when a kill fails, for example because the process already exited or permission was denied, so that I know the real state.
14. As an OMP user, I want processes started through OMP's supervised launches (hub launches, the browser tool's Chromium, LSP) attributed to their owning Agent Session, so that the list is correct even when OMP did not start them from bash.
15. As an OMP user, I want processes the agent started from bash, including ones put in the background with `&` or `nohup`, attributed to their Agent Session, so that the servers that actually hold my ports are covered.
16. As an OMP user, I want that attribution to survive after OMP exits and the process is reparented, so that the leftovers I care about are still identifiable.
17. As an OMP user, I want processes started before this feature was installed shown as unknown origin, not guessed, so that the monitor never claims a process it cannot prove.
18. As an OMP user, I want a Status Segment like `⚠ 2 ports` in the Shared Display whenever Leftover Processes hold ports, so that I notice leftovers without running a command.
19. As an OMP user, I want that segment hidden when there are none, so that it costs no space normally.
20. As an OMP user, I want the segment to update when a turn starts and about every 30 seconds while idle, so that a server left running between turns still shows up.
21. As an OMP user, I want the segment to fall back to OMP's native status when no Display Host is running, like other Display Producers, so that it works without Shared Display.
22. As an OMP user, I want to hide or show the segment through display configuration, like other segments, so that I control my status line.
23. As an OMP user, I want to be asked, when I start or switch to another Agent Session, whether to close the processes the previous session left running, so that cleanup happens at the natural moment.
24. As an OMP user, I want that prompt to list exactly the processes that session started and to offer "close all" or "keep", so that I keep the ones I still need.
25. As an OMP user, I want the next OMP start to tell me about Leftover Processes from the session I quit, when OMP could not ask at exit, so that nothing is silently forgotten.
26. As an OMP user, I want no prompt and no notice when a session left nothing running, so that the feature stays quiet.
27. As an OMP user, I want `/procs` to work even when OMP's daemon broker for a project is not running, so that leftovers from crashed sessions are still found.
28. As an OMP user, I want the bash tag to work together with RTK's command rewriting, so that enabling both features never breaks a command.
29. As an OMP user, I want the bash tag to leave the command's behavior unchanged, so that adding attribution never changes what my commands do.
30. As a plugin maintainer, I want the attribution rules in one documented decision (ADR-0010), so that nobody removes the bash tag without knowing why it exists.
31. As an OMP user without a UI (print or RPC mode), I want `/procs` to return a plain-text listing instead of an overlay, so that the command is still useful.
32. As an OMP user, I want the monitor to stay read-only until I confirm a kill, so that opening `/procs` never changes anything.

## Implementation Decisions

- **New feature.** It is named `process-monitor` and is a new workspace package exposed as an omp-plugins root feature, like `rtk` and `beads`. It registers the `/procs` command and publishes one Status Segment under the source name `process-monitor`.
- **Bash tagging (ADR-0010).** On every bash tool call, the feature prefixes the command so that its environment carries `OMP_PLUGINS_SESSION=<Agent Session id>`. The prefix composes with RTK's rewrite: whichever runs, the marker ends outermost and applies to the whole command. The command's own text is otherwise untouched. Subagents run in the same process with their own session ids, so the marker uses the session id of the agent that issued the call and never mutates process-wide environment.
- **Attribution sources, in precedence order:**
  1. **Supervised launches.** These come from OMP's own `omp ps --all --json` output, which carries the daemon name, state, PID, command and `owner` session id for each supervised process, including scopes whose broker has exited. Daemon spec files carry full environment snapshots and can contain secrets, so they are never read.
  2. **Tagged processes.** These are processes whose environment carries `OMP_PLUGINS_SESSION`, read from the OS process table.
  3. **OMP internals.** These are OMP's own worker processes, such as the broker and the eval workers, shown in their own collapsed group.
  4. **Unknown origin.** This is every other process holding a listening TCP port. It is view-only.
- **Ports.** Ports come from the OS list of listening TCP sockets, mapped by PID. A process with no listening port is still listed if it is attributed.
- **Agent Session ended.** A session counts as ended when no live OMP process holds it, based on OMP's per-session owner locks. A process whose session has ended is a Leftover Process.
- **External boundary.** Every external read and every kill goes through the extension's injected exec. That covers `omp ps`, the process table, the socket list and the kill itself. The feature never calls OS process APIs directly, so tests can replace the whole outside world at one point. A kill always targets one numeric PID and is only offered for categories 1 and 2.
- **Overlay.** This is a Read-only Status Overlay with a scrollable list, grouped by project. The current project comes first, then the internals group, then the unknown-origin group. Selecting a row and confirming kills it. Enter/Esc closes the overlay without touching prompt input.
- **Segment.** It shows the count of Leftover Processes holding at least one port, rendered from a template with a `{count}` token that defaults to `⚠ {count} ports`. It publishes nothing at zero. It refreshes on turn start and on a roughly 30-second timer while idle, and the timer stops on session shutdown. It follows the existing display visibility configuration pattern.
- **Session-end prompt.**
  - On switching to or starting another Agent Session while the UI is available, the feature asks about that session's still-running processes. "Close all" kills each one by PID. "Keep" leaves them.
  - When the session ends because OMP quits, it records the session id. On the next start, it notifies about that session's Leftover Processes, if any are still running.
  - Whether a confirmation can be shown during shutdown is to be verified during implementation. The fallback is the next-start notice.
- **No-UI mode.** `/procs` returns the same grouping as plain text.

## Testing Decisions

- **What a good test is.** It drives the extension the way OMP does and asserts only what a user or another feature can observe:
  - the rewritten bash command;
  - the published Status Segment;
  - overlay and notification text;
  - the kill commands issued through exec.
- **Seam.** The extension's default export, driven by a fake `pi`: events, commands, the event bus, and an `exec` that answers `omp ps --all --json`, the process table and the socket list with fixtures. A disposable HOME and project directory complete it. The clock is injected through extension options, so the idle refresh can be tested.
- **Cases to cover:**
  - Tagging, with and without RTK's rewrite present.
  - Attribution precedence.
  - Leftover Process detection when the session has ended.
  - Unknown-origin rows offer no kill.
  - Kill sends exactly one PID and only after confirmation.
  - Kill failure is reported.
  - The segment count and its hiding at zero.
  - The session-switch prompt, and the next-start notice after a quit.
  - A scope whose broker has exited.
- **Prior art.** The RTK extension tests (bash `tool_call` rewriting, Shared Display snapshots, session lifecycle) and the Beads command-menu tests (overlay and command behavior with exec fixtures).
- **Smoke proof.** The `verify-omp-plugins` skill drives `/procs` in the real TUI. Add a `/procs` entry to its feature map.

## Out of Scope

- A web dashboard. It would itself hold a port.
- A standalone shell CLI outside OMP.
- Killing processes of unknown origin, or killing by process name.
- Changing OMP core or its daemon broker.
- Attributing processes that were started before the feature was installed.
- Restarting processes or showing their logs. OMP's own `omp ps logs/restart` already covers supervised ones.

## Further Notes

- Glossary terms used: Agent Session, Leftover Process, Status Segment, Shared Display, Display Host, Display Producer, Read-only Status Overlay. See ADR-0010 for the bash tag.
- Suggested build order across the three new features: process-monitor first, then the Beads live view, then skill-stats. There are no hard dependencies between them.
- Bump the version of every package touched, as the repository rules require.

title: pstack: GitHub release branch distribution with CI and release workflows
description:
## Parent

omp-plugins-4nv

## What to build

The owner chose a GitHub release branch instead of npm. pstack installs with:

```
omp plugin install github:seenark/omp-plugins#release/pstack
```

or a pinned tag `#pstack-v<version>`.

- **Release build.** A deterministic release build turns `packages/pstack` into a self-contained plugin tree.
  - It ships `skills/`, `agents/`, README, notices and licenses.
  - The extension is bundled with every `@codesook/*` import inlined, because none are on npm. `@oh-my-pi/*` stays external, since the OMP host provides it.
  - Any runtime file a skill references by path still resolves at that path. Example: the verdict helper that `panel-verdicts.md` imports from `<skill dir>/../../src/verdict.ts`.
  - The release `package.json` has no `dependencies`; `@oh-my-pi/*` are peers. It keeps the `omp` key, with extensions pointing at the bundle.
  - The sync engine, tests and dev tooling are left out of the release tree.
- **CI.** Runs on every pull request and every push to main: frozen-lockfile install, then `bun run verify`.
- **Release.** Runs on push to main and on manual dispatch. When `packages/pstack/package.json` has a version that has no `pstack-v<version>` tag yet, it:
  1. builds the release;
  2. commits it to the `release/pstack` branch, which has no main-branch history;
  3. creates the tag `pstack-v<version>`.

  Re-running with an unchanged version does nothing. Releasing is driven by the existing version-bump rule.
- **npm cut over.** The pstack npm publish path is removed: drop `publish:pstack` and pstack's entry in `publish:all`. Install docs (pstack README, root README, setup guide, ADR-0008 if it mentions npm) describe the GitHub install, upgrading, and how to cut a release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The release build output has no `@codesook/` import, and its `package.json` has no `dependencies`.
- [ ] Building twice from the same commit gives byte-identical trees.
- [ ] The built tree, linked into an isolated OMP 18.11.1 HOME, serves `skill://bro`, discovers the pstack agents, and runs `/pstack status`.
- [ ] Same check: `/poteto` publishes the Status Segment and suspends Caveman and Ponytail, with `github:seenark/omp-plugins` (main) providing those.
- [ ] The verdict helper import path from `panel-verdicts.md` resolves in the built tree.
- [ ] The workflows pass actionlint (or an equivalent syntax check).
- [ ] The release job is idempotent for an unchanged version, which is shown with a dry-run mode or a test of the version/tag decision.
- [ ] `bun run verify` passes.

description:

title: /pstack setup: guided model role configuration
description:
## Parent

- **Safety.** It reads the config back and restores the snapshot on mismatch.
- **Panel rules.** It rejects two seats on the same model and warns when the panel is single-vendor.
- **Task isolation.** When OMP task isolation is off, it offers to enable it and only does so after explicit confirmation.

- [ ] A readback mismatch restores the previous config.
- [ ] Re-running with the same choices yields an identical config.

title: pstack model roles and lane agents
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Every pstack lane resolves its model through `pstack-*` model roles.
- **Generated agents.** Agents are generated from one role table:

  - for each panel seat a–e, a read-only critic and a write-capable builder. The critic returns a structured verdict: verdict plus findings with severity, file, line, claim and evidence;
  - `poteto-agent`, which autoloads poteto-mode.
- **Seat checks.** The extension resolves panel seats through the models API. A `before_subagent_spawn` handler blocks spawning an unset seat's agent, with a reason telling the agent to skip that seat.
- **Dropouts.** A model fallback inside a seat's run, observed on the parent's subagent event channel, is recorded as a dropout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generated agents match the role table. Regeneration is idempotent, and verify fails if agents drift from the table.
- [ ] With `pstack-build` unset, the build agent runs on the `@task` model.
- [ ] With `pstack-panel-b` unset, dispatching its critic is blocked with a skip-this-seat reason. With it set, the critic runs on that model.
- [ ] Read-only critics have no `edit`, `bash`, `eval` or `exec` tools.
- [ ] A fallback during a seat run produces a dropout record.
- [ ] Harness tests cover spawn block and pass, and dropout capture.
