title: pstack for OMP: @codesook/omp-pstack package
description:
## Problem Statement

I use OMP only, never Cursor, and I want Lauren Tan's pstack workflows (poteto-mode, playbooks, principles, multi-model review, real-app proof) inside OMP. The community port I had installed, `omp-pstack`, got in the way more than it helped, so I uninstalled it:

- It tracked an old Upstream (pstack 0.14.5), while Upstream is now 0.15.25 with new skills and principles.
- Its model lanes were named after OMP's built-in agent roles and stored concrete model selectors a second time, outside my model roles. They went stale, and its "multi-model" reviewers could silently all be the same model.
- Its setup was a long prose skill the model followed by hand, so results varied run to run, and it assumed Grok and external CLIs I do not use.
- Its rules were prose only. A read-only reviewer could still reach mutating tools, and nothing stopped `sed -i` on source.
- It was installed from a marketplace, so its `tdd` skill tied in priority with Matt Pocock's `tdd` in my `~/.agents/skills`. A pstack workflow could load the wrong skill without anyone noticing.
- It activated itself on every non-trivial task, which costs Claude quota I am rationing.
- Its state was lost when compaction ran.
- Its reply rules fought my Caveman and Ponytail Instruction Modes.

Cursor-only parts (cloud agents, Bugbot naming, Graphite stacks, `/loop`, Routines) leaked into workflows I cannot run.

My budget is Claude-only for now. Codex comes back in about two months, and adding it back should take one command, not a reconfiguration.

## Solution

A new workspace package in this monorepo, `@codesook/omp-pstack`. It is published to npm and installed with `omp plugin install @codesook/omp-pstack`.

- **Content.** It carries pstack as Vendored Content from the Upstream `cursor/plugins` pstack component at a recorded Pinned Revision. Scripted Adaptations point every Cursor primitive at its OMP equivalent, and Cursor-only parts are Excluded.
- **Activation.** pstack does nothing until I start it. `/poteto <task>` starts poteto-mode for the Agent Session. For that session it switches Caveman and Ponytail off, and it shows a pstack Status Segment on the Shared Display.
- **Models.** Every pstack lane resolves its model through `pstack-*` model roles in my OMP config.
  - `/pstack setup` lets me pick those models from menus. Each role explains what it is, when it runs, and what kind of model suits it.
  - It probes each choice before saving and never touches my other roles.
  - Panels have 1 to 5 seats. An unset seat is simply absent.
  - Presets switch between Claude-only and Claude plus Codex.
- **Guards.** Three layers. Read-only lanes get no mutating tools at all. A hook blocks damaging commands before they run. Style issues get warnings only.
- **Settings.** pstack behavior settings appear in `/omp-plugins`.
- **Upstream updates.** A sync script plus an agent guideline let OMP itself update pstack from Upstream, stopping to ask me only on structural changes.

## User Stories

1. As an OMP user, I want to install pstack with `omp plugin install @codesook/omp-pstack`, so that it installs like my other Codesook plugins.
2. As an OMP user, I want pstack to do nothing until I invoke it, so that ordinary work does not spend extra quota on panels.
3. As an OMP user, I want `/poteto <task>`, so that I can start poteto-mode on a task with one command.
4. As an OMP user, I want `/skill:poteto-mode` to have the same effect as `/poteto`, so that both entry points behave identically.
5. As an OMP user, I want to call any pstack skill directly with `/skill:<name>`, such as `how`, `why`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `bro`, or `pstack-teach`, so that I can use one workflow without the full poteto-mode run.
6. As an OMP user, I want every Upstream pstack skill except `make-bot-ui`, including standalone skills that no workflow calls (`teach`, `bro`, `sharpen`, `in-your-own-words`, `correct`, `blast-radius`, `recall`, `automate-me`, `poteto-help`, `maintain-verification-skill`), so that nothing useful is missing.
7. As an OMP user, I want the 24 principle skills hidden from the skill list but still readable, so that my prompt stays small while workflows can load them.
8. As an OMP user, I want pstack's TDD skill to be named `pstack-tdd`, so that I can tell it apart from Matt Pocock's `tdd`.
9. As an OMP user, I want pstack's teach skill to be named `pstack-teach`, so that Matt Pocock's `teach` keeps its plain name.
10. As a pstack workflow, I want every reference to a renamed skill rewritten to its new name, so that bug-fix always loads `pstack-tdd` and never another `tdd`.
11. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack doctor` to warn me when a skill name a pstack workflow calls resolves to a skill from another source, so that a future collision is caught.
12. As an OMP user, I want Caveman switched off for the rest of the Agent Session once pstack starts, so that its terse style does not fight pstack's reply rules.
13. As an OMP user, I want Ponytail switched off for the rest of the Agent Session once pstack starts, so that its `shortcut:` comments and closing lines do not fight pstack's no-comments and checkpoint rules.
14. As an OMP user, I want that switch-off to apply to the current Agent Session only, so that my other sessions keep Caveman and Ponytail at their configured Mode Level.
15. As an OMP user, I want to turn Caveman or Ponytail back on with their own commands mid-session, so that I keep control.
16. As an OMP user, I want settings to choose whether pstack switches Caveman and Ponytail off, so that I can change my mind without code changes.
17. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack setup` to list only models my OMP registry can serve, so that I never see Grok or providers I do not have.
18. As an OMP user, I want each role in `/pstack setup` to show what it is, when it is used, and what kind of model it should get, so that I remember months later.
19. As an OMP user, I want presets (`claude-only`, `claude-codex`, `lean`), so that one choice fills every role sensibly.
20. As an OMP user, I want to adjust individual roles after picking a preset, so that I can tune one role without redoing everything.
21. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack setup` to probe every selected model before saving, so that a model I cannot reach is never written.
22. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack setup` to write only `pstack-*` model roles, so that my `default`, `commit`, `vision`, `tiny`, and `advisor` roles stay exactly as I set them.
23. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack setup` to read the config back after writing and restore it on mismatch, so that a bad write cannot corrupt my config.
24. As an OMP user, I want running `/pstack setup` again with the same choices to produce an identical config, so that reruns are safe.
25. As an OMP user, I want to edit `pstack-*` roles by hand in my OMP config if I prefer, so that setup is a convenience and not a requirement.
26. As an OMP user, I want work roles that I have not set to fall back to OMP's built-in roles, so that pstack works before I run setup.
27. As an OMP user, I want panel seats from 1 to 5, so that I can run a small Claude-only panel now and add Codex later.
28. As an OMP user, I want an unset panel seat treated as absent, not as a failure, so that a 3-seat panel is normal.
29. As an OMP user, I want a panel seat whose model falls back to another model during a run recorded as a dropout, so that a panel never pretends to be diverse.
30. As an OMP user, I want setup and doctor to refuse two seats with the same model, so that every seat adds a different view.
31. As an OMP user, I want every panel verdict to state "diversity reduced: single vendor" when all seats share a vendor, so that Claude-only reviews are honest about their limits.
32. As an OMP user, I want a maximum-panel-size setting, so that I can cap quota spend per review without deleting roles.
33. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack preset claude-codex` to verify Codex first, then add a Codex seat and move the final judge to Codex, so that re-enabling Codex is one step.
34. As an OMP user, I want read-only pstack lanes (critics, explorers, security) to have no edit, write, bash, or eval tools, so that they physically cannot change files.
35. As an OMP user, I want `sed -i` and `perl -i` on tracked source blocked before they run, with a reason pointing at the edit tool, so that files are never damaged and the agent continues without restarting its answer.
36. As an OMP user, I want any mutating tool call from a read-only pstack lane blocked as a second line of defense, so that a misconfigured agent definition cannot slip through.
37. As an OMP user, I want pstack lanes blocked from spawning their own subagents, so that the parent keeps control of routing and cost.
38. As an OMP user, I want style problems (narrating comments, a missing throughput checkpoint, a todolist missing playbook steps, claiming done without runtime proof) raised as warnings rather than blocks, so that I keep the signal without the cost of aborted answers.
39. As an OMP user, I want guard strictness settings (block and warn, warn only, off), so that I can relax enforcement when it gets in the way.
40. As an OMP user, I want guards to apply only in Agent Sessions where pstack is active, and always to pstack lanes, so that my non-pstack work is untouched.
41. As an OMP user, I want a pstack Status Segment on the Shared Display showing the playbook, step progress, and panel attendance, so that I can see where a run is at a glance.
42. As an OMP user, I want no pstack Status Segment in sessions where pstack is not active, so that the display stays clean.
43. As an OMP user, I want pstack's run state (active flag, playbook, step, panel receipts) to survive compaction and session resume, so that long runs do not lose their place.
44. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack status` to show the current run state, so that I can check without reading the transcript.
45. As an OMP user, I want `/pstack doctor` to check role coverage, panel rules, skill-name ownership, Instruction Mode wiring, and Display Host availability, so that one command tells me whether pstack is healthy.
46. As an OMP user, I want a pstack page in `/omp-plugins` (suspend Caveman, suspend Ponytail, maximum panel size, guard strictness, and a shortcut to model role setup), so that all Codesook settings live in one place.
47. As an OMP user, I want the `/omp-plugins` pstack page to say the plugin is not installed when it is missing, so that the menu stays consistent with other optional plugins.
48. As an OMP user, I want workflows that used Cursor cloud agents to run as local background tasks in isolated worktrees, so that swarm, arena, orchestrate, and autopilot still work on my machine.
49. As an OMP user, I want "run until done" and goal-style workflows mapped to OMP's goal mode, so that I use OMP's native mechanism.
50. As an OMP user, I want PR-watching workflows to use OMP's GitHub tool and background waits instead of Cursor's `/loop`, so that babysit and shipping work without Cursor.
51. As an OMP user, I want Graphite-dependent steps replaced with `gh`, so that shipping works without a tool I do not use.
52. As an OMP user, I want Bugbot-specific wording generalized to any review bot, so that the skeptical triage posture applies to the bots I actually have.
53. As an OMP user, I want transcript, skill, and MCP references pointed at OMP's equivalents (`history://`, OMP sessions, `skill://`, `mcp://`), so that recall, reflect, and automate-me read real data.
54. As an OMP user, I want `control-cli` and `control-ui` mapped to OMP's bash (PTY or managed service) and browser tool, so that real-app proof works.
55. As an OMP user, I want to say "update pstack from Upstream" in OMP, and have OMP follow a written guideline, so that I do not run updates myself.
56. As a maintainer agent, I want a sync script that fetches Upstream at a target revision, applies the Adaptation table, merges against recorded forks, and reports, so that the mechanical part of an update is deterministic.
57. As a maintainer agent, I want a fork registry recording every intentionally changed path with its reason, so that I know which differences from Upstream are deliberate.
58. As a maintainer agent, I want the sync to fail on any leftover Cursor-specific term, so that no Cursor-only instruction slips into a release.
59. As a maintainer agent, I want the guideline to tell me to stop and ask the owner when a skill or playbook is added, removed, or renamed, a new Cursor primitive appears, a new skill-name collision appears, or the license changes, so that structural changes get a human decision.
60. As a maintainer agent, I want to continue without asking when an update only changes wording, so that routine syncs are fast.
61. As a maintainer agent, I want CI or verify to fail when a vendored file differs from Upstream without a fork registry entry, so that silent drift is impossible.
62. As a maintainer agent, I want each new Upstream skill classified as workflow-called, standalone, or Cursor-only, so that its inclusion decision is explicit.
63. As an OMP user, I want the package README to state the tracked pstack version and Pinned Revision, so that I know which Upstream I am running.
64. As an OMP user, I want correct MIT attribution for Lauren Tan, Cursor, and any ideas taken from `omp-pstack` or `pstack-claude`, so that licensing is clean.
65. As an OMP user, I want `bun run verify` to cover the new package, so that one command validates the monorepo.

## Implementation Decisions

**Baseline and package**

- **OMP baseline.** The OMP baseline is 18.11.1. Every OMP behavior the plan relies on was checked against OMP source at tag v18.11.1 (HEAD `a536558`); see "Verified against OMP 18.11.1" below.
- **Package.** A new workspace package published as `@codesook/omp-pstack`, laid out like the Ponytail package, with OMP peer dependency ≥ 18.11.1. It depends on the Shared Display client like other Display Producers.
- **Publishing.** It gets its own publish script and joins the all-packages publish.
- **Not a root feature.** It is not added to the root package's `omp.features`. Features gate extensions only, not skills, agents, or rules, and installing the package separately while also listing it as a root feature would load the extension twice.
- **Discovery.** The package root ships `skills/`, `agents/`, and `rules/` for native discovery by OMP's `omp-plugins` provider (priority 90). Its `package.json` must carry an `omp` key, or OMP skips the root entirely. The package must not ship an Agent Plugins `plugin.json`, which would move skills to another provider. There is no always-apply mandate rule, because activation is manual only.
- **Rule names.** Rule files are named `pstack-<name>`. Rules have no namespace, and a same-named rule from a higher-priority source silently replaces ours.

**Vendored Content and Adaptations**

- **Upstream and pin.** Upstream is the `cursor/plugins` pstack component. The initial Pinned Revision is pstack 0.15.25, commit `f713f14203cd6420cec13cd7c55c32d598dbab68`. `deslop` comes from the same repository's cursor-team-kit component at the same pin, because Upstream playbooks call it.
- **Included.** All 54 Upstream pstack skills except `make-bot-ui`, every playbook and reference, and the `poteto-agent` and `comment-sicko` agents.
- **Excluded.**
  - `make-bot-ui`.
  - `automations/benny` and `docs/guide`.
  - Sticky-mode frontmatter.
  - The separate thermos plugin, and every other cursor-team-kit skill.
  - The external provider runner (claude, codex, and Grok CLIs).
  - Graphite.
- **How Adaptations are recorded.** They live in an ordered substitution table, where each rule carries a rationale, plus a fork registry of intentionally diverged paths (path, kind, reason, since). This extends the Vendored Content process in the Upstream-sync guide: Caveman and Ponytail list their Adaptations in the README, but pstack's volume needs a scripted table. Consider recording this as an ADR.
- **Adaptation mapping.**
  - Cursor `Task` / `subagent_type` → OMP `task` with a named agent.
  - `AskQuestion` → `ask`.
  - Cloud agents → background tasks with isolation.
  - `/goal` and "run until done" → OMP goal mode (`/goal set <objective>`). Extensions cannot start a goal, so playbooks tell the user to start it.
  - `/loop` PR polling → the GitHub tool's run watch, or async bash plus wait.
  - Cursor transcript, skill, and MCP paths → `history://`, OMP sessions, `skill://`, `mcp://`.
  - `control-cli` / `control-ui` → bash (PTY or managed service) and the browser tool.
  - Bugbot → generic review bot (the triage reference is kept).
  - Graphite → `gh` (auto-merge with head-commit match, base-chained PRs). Autopilot-stack is degraded, and that is recorded as a fork.
  - The provider-dispatch reference is rewritten for pstack model roles.
- **Skill naming.** Upstream names are kept. A name that collides with another discovered skill on this machine is renamed `pstack-<name>`, with all references rewritten through the substitution table. Initial renames are `tdd` → `pstack-tdd` and `teach` → `pstack-teach`. Namespaced names containing `/` are rejected by OMP and cannot be chosen.
- **Visibility.** Principle skills are hidden from the prompt list. Standalone skills stay visible.
- **Bundled scripts.**
  - `watch-pr` is replaced by the GitHub tool.
  - `check-plan` is replaced by the todo guard (see Guards).
  - `orch`, `worktree-audit`, and show-me-your-work's log script are vendored as-is.

**Model roles**

- **Role names.** This is a contract and is costly to change later.

  | Role | Fallback when unset |
  |---|---|
  | `pstack-explore` | `@smol` |
  | `pstack-build` | `@task` |
  | `pstack-mechanical` | `@tiny` |
  | `pstack-design` | `@designer` |
  | `pstack-judge` | `@slow` |
  | `pstack-security` | `@slow` |
  | `pstack-panel-a` … `pstack-panel-e` | none; an unset seat is absent |

- **Agent definitions.** Agents reference roles through their frontmatter model list. `task.agentModelOverrides` is not used.
- **Panel agents.** Each seat has two agents:
  - A read-only critic that returns a structured verdict (verdict plus findings with severity, file, line, claim, evidence).
  - A write-capable builder, dispatched only with task isolation.
- **Panel rules.**
  - At most 5 seats, capped further by the maximum-panel-size setting.
  - No duplicate model across seats.
  - A single-vendor panel's verdict states "diversity reduced: single vendor".
  - A fallback during a panel run is recorded as a dropout. Child fallbacks are observed on the parent EventBus `task:subagent:event` channel.
- **Unset seats.** OMP does not skip an unset single-alias role; the child fails with "No model selected" on its first prompt. pstack therefore owns seat absence:
  - On activation it resolves each seat role through the extension models API and tells the session which seats exist.
  - A `before_subagent_spawn` handler blocks any spawn of an unset seat's agent with a reason telling the agent to skip that seat.
  - Work-role agents keep a two-entry model list (pstack role, then the built-in role), which OMP resolves by skipping the unset entry.
- **`/pstack setup`.**
  - Reads the model registry and offers presets (`claude-only`, `claude-codex`, `lean`), then per-role menus with what/when/recommended text.
  - Probes each selected model with a one-turn call.
  - Writes only `pstack-*` keys in the user's model roles, plus empty fallback chains for panel seats. It writes through OMP's in-process settings API, which keeps sibling roles and flushes to the config file, not through the CLI, which only replaces the whole record.
  - Reads the result back and restores the snapshot on mismatch.
  - Is idempotent.
- **`/pstack doctor`.** Read-only checks of:
  - role coverage and panel rules;
  - skill-name ownership for every workflow-called skill;
  - Instruction Mode suspension wiring;
  - Display Host availability;
  - whether OMP task isolation is enabled, which arena and swarm writers need. It is off by default, and pstack never turns it on silently. Setup offers to enable it and asks for explicit confirmation.
- **`/pstack status`.** Shows the run state.

**Activation and Instruction Modes**

- **`/poteto <task>`.** Registered by the extension. It starts poteto-mode on the task and marks pstack active for the Agent Session. Invoking the poteto-mode skill through `/skill:poteto-mode` also activates. Detection uses the `input` event in interactive and RPC modes, and the session's `skill-prompt` custom message elsewhere.
- **Suspension contract.**
  - On activation, pstack emits a versioned EventBus message asking named Instruction Modes to suspend.
  - Caveman and Ponytail each consume it and apply a Session Override at Mode Level `off` for the rest of the Agent Session. The override is never persisted.
  - The user's own Caveman and Ponytail commands still work afterwards.
  - pstack re-emits on session start when restored state says it is active, so suspension survives resume.
- **Package releases.** Caveman and Ponytail each get a minor version bump.

**Guards**

1. **Agent tool allowlists.** Read-only lanes get `read`, `grep`, `glob`, `lsp`, and `ast_grep`. They never get `edit`, `bash`, `eval`, or `exec`. OMP auto-adds `yield`, and also a device-only `write` that is limited to `local://` and `xd://` devices. There is no `hub` tool.
2. **Extension `tool_call` hook.** It blocks before execution and returns a reason; the model continues without restarting its answer.
   - It blocks in-place stream edits on tracked source.
   - It blocks mutating calls from read-only pstack lanes, including `write` to any target other than `local://`, because the device-only `write` can reach mounted devices. Lanes are identified through the hook context's agent identity, which OMP lowercases.
   - It blocks lane-initiated spawns.
   - It checks a todo `init` against the active playbook's steps and adds a warning when steps are missing.
3. **Non-blocking warnings.** Narrating comments, a missing throughput checkpoint, and a done claim without runtime proof are raised through tool-result context, non-interrupting rules, or the stop hook.

- **Scope.** Interrupting stream rules are not used. Guards apply only in Agent Sessions where pstack is active, and always to pstack lanes. Extensions run inside subagent sessions, so lane tool calls reach the same hook. `tool_call` fails closed on a handler error or timeout. `before_subagent_spawn` fails open, so it is never the only guard.
- **Strictness setting.** Block and warn (default), warn only, or off.

**State and display**

- **Run state.** Active flag, playbook, step progress, and panel receipts are stored as reverse-domain custom session entries and rebuilt from the session branch on session start and resume. Compaction does not remove them. The compaction hook's preserve data is not used: OMP keeps only the last handler's result, so other plugins could overwrite it. After compaction, pstack injects a short hidden reminder of the active playbook and step so the model keeps its place.
- **Display.** pstack is a Display Producer publishing one Status Segment, for example `pstack · feature · 3/7 · panel 3/4`. It publishes a tombstone when inactive, as ADR-0003 specifies.

**Settings**

- A Behavior Configuration section for pstack in the Root Plugin Configuration, with these fields:
  - suspend Caveman (default on);
  - suspend Ponytail (default on);
  - maximum panel size, 1 to 5;
  - guard strictness.
- The `/omp-plugins` dialog gains a pstack page that follows ADR-0004 (staged draft, Apply emits the config-changed event, a missing plugin is reported). Model roles are not stored there; the page links to `/pstack setup`.

**Upstream sync**

- **Sync script.** It fetches Upstream at the target revision, applies the substitution table, 3-way merges against the fork registry, scans for Cursor-specific terms, checks skill-name collisions, and writes a report.
- **Verify.** `bun run verify` fails on undeclared drift from the Pinned Revision.
- **Guideline.** The Upstream-sync agent guide gains a pstack entry with stop-and-ask conditions, and the AGENTS.md pointer names pstack. No new skill is created for this.

**Verified against OMP 18.11.1**

Checked in OMP source at tag v18.11.1 (HEAD `a536558`). Changes between 18.10.4 and 18.11.1 in these areas only help the plan:

- `autoloadSkills` now rediscovers skills the session has not seen yet (#15723).
- Agent frontmatter gained `structured`.
- An empty `tools` value now means no tools.
- `/plugins enable|disable` refreshes npm plugins' skills and agents.
- `omp plugin install` no longer needs Bun on `PATH`.

- An npm-installed plugin root is scanned for skills, rules, and agents. Confirmed. It requires an `omp` key in `package.json`.
- The `omp-plugins` provider (90) outranks `~/.agents/skills` (70). Confirmed. The loser of a collision becomes `agents/<name>`, and bare names and `skill://` resolve to the winner. Native user and project skills (100), skillshare (95), and `skills.customDirectories` outrank pstack, which is why doctor checks skill-name ownership.
- Skill names containing `/` are rejected. `hide` keeps `skill://` and `/skill:` working. A missing `description` silently drops a skill. All confirmed.
- Rule frontmatter (`condition`, `scope`, `agents`, `interruptMode`, `astCondition`, `question`) and `omp ttsr test` fixtures. Confirmed.
- npm-installed plugin agents keep frontmatter `model` role aliases. Confirmed.
- An agent model list skips an unset custom role. Confirmed for lists. A single unset role is refuted: the spawn fails instead, which is handled under "Unset seats".
- Custom role names and `retry.fallbackChains.<role>: []`. Confirmed, for single-pattern agents.
- Lane tool surface. Confirmed, with the device-only `write` addition handled in the guards. No `hub`.
- `tool_call` block returns an error tool result with the reason and continues the turn, failing closed. Confirmed.
- `before_subagent_spawn` payload is agent, invocation kind, model role, patterns, and spawn key, with no task text. It returns model, block, reason, or note, and fails open. Confirmed.
- One EventBus per Agent Session, shared by all extensions regardless of package. Confirmed. Subagents get their own bus, and child events are mirrored to the parent.
- Model roles are writable. Confirmed, through the in-process settings API or a whole-record CLI set.
- `/goal` exists in interactive mode. Confirmed. There is no extension API to start a goal.

## Testing Decisions

- **What a good test is.** It drives external behavior through the package's public entry and observes outcomes: registered commands, blocked or allowed tool calls, emitted EventBus messages, Shared Display snapshots, persisted session entries, and written config. Tests never assert prose wording, vendored file text, or internal helpers. Every guard has a must-trip fixture and a must-pass fixture, because a check that matches nothing looks like a pass.
- **Seam 1: extension.** The pstack extension's default export runs against a fake ExtensionAPI harness (handlers, commands, EventBus, session entries, UI). Prior art is the Ponytail and Caveman extension tests. It covers:
  - `/poteto` activation and `/skill:poteto-mode` activation;
  - the Instruction Mode suspend message;
  - Status Segment publish and tombstone;
  - state restore across `session_start` and compaction;
  - every `tool_call` guard, block and pass;
  - strictness levels;
  - `/pstack setup` against a fake registry and fake config writer (probe failure writes nothing, rerun is idempotent, non-pstack roles are untouched, readback mismatch restores);
  - `/pstack doctor` findings (duplicate seat, single vendor, foreign skill owning a workflow-called name);
  - live settings updates.
- **Seam 2: sync.** The sync script runs over a fixture Upstream tree. It covers substitutions applied, forks preserved, a conflict reported, a leftover Cursor term failing, a collision renamed with references rewritten, an Excluded path absent, and undeclared drift failing.
- **Seam 3: rules.** Every shipped OMP rule has must-trip and must-pass cases run through `omp ttsr test`.
- **Existing seams extended.**
  - The Caveman and Ponytail extension tests gain cases for the suspension message: Session Override `off`, not persisted, user command re-enables.
  - The root settings tests gain the pstack page: staged draft, Apply event, missing-plugin state.
- **Acceptance smoke (verification, not a permanent test).**
  - `bun run verify` passes.
  - In a fresh OMP 18.11.1 session with the package installed, `/poteto` runs a small feature end to end.
  - The panel seats resolve to distinct models.
  - Caveman and Ponytail are off for that session only.
  - The Status Segment appears and survives `/compact`.
  - A read-only lane cannot write.

## Out of Scope

- The external provider runner, Grok, and any codex, claude, or grok CLI lanes.
- The thermos plugin, and cursor-team-kit skills other than `deslop`.
- `make-bot-ui`, `automations/benny`, the Upstream `docs/guide`, and sticky mode.
- Graphite, and full stacked-PR tooling beyond base-chained PRs with `gh`.
- Changing any non-pstack model role (`default`, `commit`, `vision`, `tiny`, `advisor`, and so on). The owner manages those.
- Automatic activation of poteto-mode on non-trivial tasks.
- Runtimes other than OMP (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Pi).
- Formal models (Lean or TLA+) of polling or scheduling.
- Committing, pushing, publishing to npm, or Dolt sync without explicit owner authority.

## Further Notes

- **Old port removed.** The previous `omp-pstack` install, its marketplace, and its `task.agentModelOverrides` rows were already removed. A backup is at `~/.omp/backup-pstack-20261016-113359/`.
- **pstack-claude.** Several ideas come from `michael-denyer/pstack-claude` and need attribution:
  - the fork registry and sync tooling;
  - the max-5, no-duplicate, single-vendor panel rules;
  - the must-trip fixture rule.

  Several skills once thought to be pstack-claude extras (`correct`, `ketchup`, `sharpen`, `in-your-own-words`, `poteto-help`, `benchmark-checklist`, and two new principles) are in Upstream 0.15.25 and arrive through vendoring.
- **ADRs.** The plan follows ADR-0003 (Display Producer over the EventBus) and ADR-0004 (root `/omp-plugins` settings, feature-owned commands). Candidate new ADRs:
  - model roles through OMP's `modelRoles` with panel seats;
  - scripted Adaptations for large Vendored Content.
- **Glossary.** Candidate terms are Model Role (pstack), Panel Seat, Lane, Workflow-called versus Standalone skill, Playbook, and Fork Registry. They should be added to the glossary lazily, when implementation settles them.
- **Budget.** Claude-only today. The `claude-codex` preset is the path back when Codex returns.

title: Initialize Beads with explicit mode and hook choices
description:
## What to build

Add explicit Beads initialization with user-controlled standard/team versus stealth mode and opt-in Git hooks. The resulting workspace is detected by the plugin without generating agent files, changing shared integration policy, or silently replacing existing issue data.

Follow the confirmed CodeGraph and Beads Plugin Design and the domain glossary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Beads init operation checks for an applicable initialized Tool Workspace before creating data. Existing workspaces are reused without destructive reinitialization, history replacement, or changes to existing hooks.
- [ ] For new initialization, let the user select standard/team or stealth mode before invoking the CLI, defaulting to standard/team. Offer supported Git-hook installation, off by default; respect upstream stealth restrictions.
- [ ] Always skip agent-file generation and other-agent setup. Skip Git-hook installation unless the user explicitly approves supported hook behavior.
- [ ] Cancelling the choices performs no initialization and leaves data, hooks, project policy, and repository agent files unchanged.
- [ ] New data targets the Integration Project, while existing redirected or shared workspaces continue following native Beads resolution.
